entities.summary:
The 2009–10 Croatian presidential election was a pivotal event in modern Croatian history, marking a significant shift in the country's political landscape. Taking place on December 27, 2009, this election saw the re-election of President Stjepan Mesić, but more importantly, it laid the groundwork for the eventual rise of Ivo Josipović, a prominent Croatian politician who would go on to serve as President from 2010 to 2015. The election also highlighted the ongoing struggle for power within the Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ), the country's largest and most influential political party, which has been a dominant force in Croatian politics since the country's independence from Yugoslavia in 1991.

The 2009–10 Croatian presidential election was a crucial moment in the country's transition from a post-Yugoslav state to a more stable and democratic society. The election process itself was marked by a high level of participation, with over 40% of eligible voters casting their ballots. The election also saw the emergence of new political forces, including the Social Democratic Party (SDP), which would go on to play a major role in Croatian politics in the years to come.

The legacy of the 2009–10 Croatian presidential election can be seen in the ongoing struggle for power within the HDZ and the eventual rise of Ivo Josipović to the presidency. The election also marked a significant shift in the country's foreign policy, as Croatia began to move closer to the European Union and away from its traditional allies in the region. The election's impact can also be seen in the ongoing development of Croatian politics, as the country continues to navigate its complex relationships with its neighbors and the wider European community.
